summary: Frederick County, MD tower for the city's forest: a 60-foot steel tower, dated to 1926 by the state and 1930 by the register; listed as gone, and no removal date found.

facts.status_note: Listed as gone; no source read gives when or why it came down

staffing.status: towerman named in April 1932; no later staffing found in sources read

facts.agency: Maryland Department of Forestry, in cooperation with the City of Frederick

events.note: State fiscal-1930 report: a 60-foot steel tower was erected and ready for service in 1926
Build year given in the register's Built field; the register ties the tower to the City of Frederick's 1930 water-supply work. Conflicts with the 1926 state report.
Tower equipped and operated for the city forest, with state forestry cooperating with the city
R.H. Wempe of Highfield, Washington County, appointed towerman

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The state's fiscal-1930 report, quoted on the weebly transcription, puts the erection in 1926. The register's Built field gives 1930, and its description ties the tower to the city's 1930 water-supply work. Both are kept in the events; the story reports both dates and says they differ.

sources.title: Hamburg
sources.publisher: Forest Lookouts (transcribed state reports and newspaper items)

notes_for_editor: Thin record. No source read gives the removal date, cause, or what remains at the site, so fate and today are both short. The build year conflicts (1926 state report vs 1930 register); the register's Built field (1930) is quoted as 'Built 1930' in the evidence, and the story states that the two dates disagree. The Hamburg Road location (Fishing Creek area) came from a legislative-district map in search results that was not read, so it is not used. A Maryland DNR fire-tower poster and Barbara Garner's 2012 book are cited as sources in search results; the DNR poster was unreachable (404) and the book was not checked.
